headline: AI sell-off drags Wall Street into correction; Trump threatens datacenter penalties
at_a_glance: US stocks closed in correction after Anthropic's rocky IPO debut and a sharp Nvidia sell-off; VIX jumped 26%.
Trump threatened 'tremendous penalties' on US firms building AI data centers abroad, with no policy details given.
Iran-linked tensions widened: tanker incidents near Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Iraqi forces entering a militia stronghold.
Russia faced accusations of a Poland airspace violation, a Denmark assassination plot, and a drone strike on a Baltic cargo ship.
The EU and UK signed a post-Brexit 'reset' deal on trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit.
market_analysis:
US stocks sold off sharply on Friday, with the S&P 500 falling 3.70% to 6,910.39 and the Dow Jones down 1.93% to 48,147.33, both closing in correction territory roughly 10% below their records. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% to 22,617.73, erasing its entire 2026 gain, as Anthropic's stock tumbled on its second day of trading and Nvidia fell further, capping its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. The VIX jumped 26.20% to 35.89 and the 10-year Treasury yield fell 14 basis points to 4.91% as investors sought safer assets. Chip stocks as a group lost roughly $2.3 trillion in value over the week.

Asian markets followed Wall Street lower: the Nikkei 225 fell 5.06% to 56,436.65, the Hang Seng dropped 1.89%, and the Shanghai Composite lost 1.22%. In Europe, the DAX fell 2.60% to 24,802.78, the Euro Stoxx 50 dropped 2.81%, and the FTSE 100 declined 1.02%, with US futures pointing to further weakness at the open (S&P 500 futures -3.64%, Nasdaq 100 futures -5.54%).

No economic data releases or earnings from the watch list are scheduled in Europe/Berlin time today. Markets remain focused on the fallout from Nvidia's reported SEC accounting probe, Trump's threat of penalties on US firms building AI data centers abroad, and the ongoing COP31 climate talks, which have run into overtime without agreement on a fossil-fuel phaseout.

mover_notes.NVDA: Shares fell amid a reported SEC probe into its accounting and a weekly AI-driven chip sell-off that erased $2.3 trillion from semiconductor stocks.
mover_notes.AMD: Fell with the broader semiconductor sell-off as chip stocks lost $2.3 trillion in value this week on AI spending concerns.
mover_notes.MU: Dropped with the week's broader chip-sector rout tied to AI spending concerns.
mover_notes.LITE: Declined alongside the broader semiconductor sell-off driven by AI spending concerns this week.

stories.title: Wall Street's AI-driven sell-off pushes S&P 500 and Dow into correction
stories.summary: On Friday the S&P 500 fell 3.70% and the Dow Jones fell 1.93%, both closing in correction territory, down 10% from their records, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% and erased its entire 2026 gain. The rout deepened after Anthropic's stock tumbled on its second day of trading following its IPO, with investors questioning the scale of AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia shares fell further, capping their longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, as chip stocks lost $2.3 trillion in value over the week. The VIX volatility index jumped 26.2% to 35.89 and the US 10-year yield fell 14 basis points to 4.91% as investors sought safety.
stories.why_it_matters: A correction across the three main US indices, led by the collapse of AI-related stocks, signals investors are reassessing the sustainability of the AI investment boom, with potential spillover to global equity and bond markets.

stories.title: Trump threatens penalties on US companies building AI data centers abroad
stories.summary: President Trump said on Friday he would impose "tremendous penalties" on American technology companies that build data centers outside the United States, though he gave no further details and said members of his own team were hearing about the policy for the first time. The threat came during a wide-ranging White House press conference in which Trump also said he has "fantastic relationships" with Putin and Xi. The announcement adds a new layer of uncertainty for AI companies already facing a sharp sell-off in their shares.
stories.why_it_matters: An unplanned threat to penalize offshore data-center investment could disrupt AI companies' global expansion plans and adds policy uncertainty just as AI-related stocks are under heavy selling pressure.

stories.title: Nvidia faces SEC accounting probe amid espionage allegations tied to China
stories.summary: Nvidia is reportedly facing a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into its accounting practices, following questions about its chip sales in Asia. Separately, Alice Huang, a woman at the center of an espionage scandal involving Nvidia, has been linked to a network of Chinese tech firms and defense contractors with ties to China's military. The news adds to pressure on Nvidia, whose shares have fallen sharply amid the broader AI sell-off following the exit of CEO Jensen Huang.
stories.why_it_matters: Regulatory scrutiny and espionage allegations compound uncertainty at one of the most important companies in the global AI supply chain, at a moment when Nvidia stock is already under heavy pressure.

stories.title: Iran war widens: tanker incidents near Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The UK's maritime agency reported two tanker incidents near Oman, and Iran said a vessel was hit by a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz; Iran also said it downed US drones over the strait. Oil shipments through Hormuz have fallen as Iranian strikes increase, with one analyst calling the recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports "increasingly fragile." Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched fresh strikes on Saudi Arabia, and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh. In Iraq, army and police units entered territory controlled by the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah for the first time in over a decade.
stories.why_it_matters: Continued attacks around the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil transit chokepoint, and the widening of Iran-linked conflicts across the region raise risks to global energy supplies and regional stability.

stories.title: Russia accused of Poland airspace violation, Denmark assassination plot, Baltic ship attack
stories.summary: Three Russian projectiles, including a suspected jet-powered drone and a missile, came down in Poland near the Ukrainian border, which NATO called a grave violation of Polish airspace. Denmark accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a US-Ukrainian rapper in Copenhagen, expelled a Russian defense attaché, and the EU's Ursula von der Leyen condemned the alleged plot. Separately, Russia said a cargo ship bound for its Kaliningrad exclave was struck by drones and set on fire in neutral waters in the Gulf of Finland. Denmark is also pushing the EU to tighten travel restrictions on Russians after a separate foiled plot.
stories.why_it_matters: A cluster of incidents involving Russia — airspace violations, an alleged assassination plot on EU soil, and an attack on shipping in the Baltic — point to rising friction between Russia and NATO members well beyond Ukraine's borders.

stories.title: EU and UK strike post-Brexit 'reset' deal on trade and youth mobility
stories.summary: The UK and the EU signed agreements at a Brussels summit aimed at reducing red tape for food exports, linking emissions trading schemes, and allowing young people to live and work more freely between the two. UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband said rejoining the EU remains "on the table" in future informal talks, while the prime minister called it "a good day for Britain and Europe." Miliband said the deal is not dependent on a separate agreement over tuition fees for EU students in Britain.
stories.why_it_matters: The agreements mark the most significant effort yet to rebuild UK-EU relations since Brexit, with potential implications for trade costs and labor mobility between the two economies.

stories.title: COP31 climate talks run into overtime as fossil-fuel phaseout remains unresolved
stories.summary: COP31 negotiations extended into overtime after nearly two weeks, with countries still divided on how to address climate change; a new draft declaration does not mention phasing out fossil fuels. China pledged to pursue rapid low-carbon electrification of its economy and said it would help other countries do the same, with Cop31 delegates being urged to commit to deriving 35% of energy from electricity by 2035.
stories.why_it_matters: A deadlock on fossil-fuel phaseout language at a major UN climate summit signals continued difficulty translating global climate commitments into binding action, with implications for energy policy and investment worldwide.

stories.title: UN talks agree to keep discussing 'killer robots' but set no binding ban
stories.summary: States at UN talks on lethal autonomous weapons agreed to continue discussions aiming to regulate such "killer robots" by 2028, extending negotiations for two years, but reached no legally binding rules or firm commitment to rein them in. The talks took place under the UN's Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons.
stories.why_it_matters: The absence of binding limits on autonomous weapons leaves a regulatory gap as militaries increasingly integrate AI into weapons systems.

stories.title: Missouri judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion Roundup settlement
stories.summary: A Missouri judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement of lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer, a deal that faced claims from roughly 65,000 people who said they developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma after using the product. The ruling is expected to resolve tens of thousands of related lawsuits in a nationwide class action.
stories.why_it_matters: The settlement removes a major legal overhang for Bayer, one of the world's largest chemical and pharmaceutical companies, after years of litigation costs.

stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI hits $3.8 billion in first-day sales, a record for entertainment
stories.summary: Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day of release, with publisher Take-Two Interactive confirming the figure. The launch is being called the biggest entertainment debut in history, surpassing the box-office run of the highest-grossing film ever. Take-Two said the game set a sales record for the industry.
stories.why_it_matters: The launch underscores the video game industry's growing weight in global entertainment spending and is a significant revenue event for Take-Two Interactive.

watch_today: Nvidia's reported SEC accounting probe and the fallout from Jensen Huang's exit are likely to stay in focus for chip stocks.
Details of Trump's threatened penalties on US companies building AI data centers abroad could emerge after his vague announcement.
COP31 negotiators continue overtime talks in search of a deal after a draft declaration omitted a fossil-fuel phaseout.
